rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Hajj time includes only part of Dhu al-Hijja, that part can be called a month for Hajj, like calling a visit time Friday when it occupies only part of Friday.
rows.anchor: وكون زمان الحج من ذي الحجة بعض هذا الشهر دون كله لا ينافي عده شهرا للحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three repetitions of Hajj use an explicit noun for a pronoun to gain concision: they mean Hajj season, the rite itself, and its time and place.
rows.anchor: فإن المراد بالحج الأول زمان الحج وبالحج الثاني نفس العمل وبالثالث زمانه ومكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Undertaking Hajj makes it obligatory upon oneself, as the command to complete Hajj and umrah indicates.
rows.anchor: وفرض الحج جعله فرضا على نفسه بالشروع فيه لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Linguistically, rafath is explicit mention of what is euphemized, fusuq departure from obedience, and jidal argumentative speech.
rows.anchor: والرفث كما مر مطلق التصريح بما يكنى عنه، والفسوق هو الخروج عن الطاعة، والجدال المراء في الكلام

rows.speaker: السنة
rows.claim: The Sunnah interprets rafath as intercourse, fusuq as lying, and jidal as saying an oath such as no, by God or yes, by God.
rows.anchor: لكن السنة فسرت الرفث بالجماع، والفسوق، بالكذب، والجدال بقول لا والله وبلى والله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder that God knows every good deed calls people to taqwa and keeps worshippers present to their work's meaning and spirit.
rows.anchor: ودعوة إلى التقوى لئلا يفقد المشتغل بطاعة الله روح الحضور ومعنى العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an joins exposition with admonition so knowledge does not separate from practice; knowledge without action has no value in Islam.
rows.anchor: لئلا يفارق العلم، والعمل، فإن العلم من غير عمل لا قيمة له في الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing command shifts from third-person reference to God's first-person speech, signaling heightened concern, nearness, and direct address.
rows.anchor: بالعدول من الغيبة إلى التكلم الذي يدل على كمال الاهتمام والاقتراب والتعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's bounty after Hajj resembles the Friday command to disperse and seek bounty; replacing the prohibition on sale with that phrase equates it with trade.
rows.anchor: فبدل البيع بالابتغاء من فضل الله فهو هو

rows.speaker: السنة
rows.claim: The Sunnah identifies seeking bounty in this verse with commerce, so the verse permits buying and selling during Hajj.
rows.anchor: ولذلك فسرت السنة الابتغاء من الفضل في هذه الآية من البيع فدلت الآية على إباحة البيع أثناء الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ifada means a group's departure from a place; the verse therefore indicates standing at Arafat and at al-Mash'ar al-Haram, which is Muzdalifa.
rows.anchor: الإفاضة هي الصدور عن المكان جماعة فهي تدل على وقوف عرفات كما تدل على الوقوف بالمشعر الحرام، وهي المزدلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God as He guided means remembering Him in a manner matching that guidance, since the people had previously been astray.
rows.anchor: أي واذكروه ذكرا يماثل هدايته إياكم وإنكم كنتم من قبل هدايته إياكم لمن الضالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent command requires departing as the people customarily did and joining the audience to them in this rite.
rows.anchor: ظاهره إيجاب الإفاضة على ما كان من دأب الناس وإلحاق المخاطبين في هذا الشأن بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This applies to Quraysh and allied Hums, who used to remain at Muzdalifa rather than Arafat, claiming they were people of the sanctuary; God ordered them to depart from Arafat with everyone else.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يقولون نحن أهل حرم الله لا نفارق الحرم فأمرهم الله سبحانه بالإفاضة من حيث أفاض الناس وهو عرفات

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says joining umrah to Hajj remains in force until Resurrection and presents tamattu as the Qur'anic and prophetic practice applicable to pilgrims.
rows.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام قال دخلت العمرة في الحج إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq explains the minimum sacrifice for tamattu as a sheep.
rows.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام في قوله تعالى { فما استيسر من الهدي } شاة

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: For a tamattu pilgrim without a sheep, al-Sadiq prescribes fasting Tarwiya eve, Tarwiya, and Arafat; late arrivals fast after Tashriq or on departure and two following days, even while traveling, all in Dhu al-Hijja.
rows.anchor: قال يصوم قبل التروية بيوم التروية ويوم عرفة

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says residents between the miqats and Mecca count as people of the Sacred Mosque and cannot perform tamattu.
rows.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام قال ما دون المواقيت إلى مكة فهو حاضري المسجد الحرام، وليس له متعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai clarifies that residents within the miqat boundaries qualify as local residents of the Sacred Mosque and thus have no tamattu; many Ahl al-Bayt reports support these rulings.
rows.anchor: أقول يعني إن ما دون المواقيت فساكنه يصدق عليه أنه من حاضري المسجد الحرام وليس له متعة

rows.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Baqir defines the Hajj months as Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'da, and Dhu al-Hijja, with no Hajj outside them.
rows.anchor: عن الباقر عليه السلام في قوله تعالى { الحج أشهر معلومات } ، قال الحج أشهر معلومات شوال

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Al-Hakim authenticated a report through Mujahid and Ata from Jabir: after objections, the Prophet defended tamattu, ordered those without sacrifice to fast three days in Hajj and seven at home, and described sacrifice sharing; Ibn Abbas adds Sa'd received a goat.
rows.anchor: أخرج الحاكم وصححه من طريق مجاهد وعطاء عن جابر قال كثرت القالة من الناس فخرجنا حجاجا

rows.speaker: عمران بن حصين
rows.claim: Imran says the tamattu verse was revealed in God's Book, they practiced it with the Prophet, and no abrogating verse or prophetic prohibition came before his death; a man then voiced his own opinion.
rows.anchor: عن عمران بن حصين قال نزلت آية المتعة في كتاب الله وفعلناها مع رسول الله

rows.speaker: عمران بن حصين
rows.claim: Mutarrif reports that Imran told him near death that the Prophet combined Hajj and umrah, with no Qur'anic abrogation or prophetic ban; a man later spoke from his own opinion.
rows.anchor: عن مطرف، قال بعث إلى عمران بن حصين في مرضه الذي توفي فيه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says tamattu is lawful and answers that the Prophet's practice takes precedence over his father's prohibition.
rows.anchor: سئل عبد الله بن عمر عن متعة الحج، قال هي حلال فقال له السائل إن أباك قد نهى عنها

rows.speaker: الضحاك بن قيس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak argues that only someone ignorant of God's command performs tamattu.
rows.anchor: فقال الضحاك لا يصنع ذلك إلا من جهل أمر الله

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: Sa'd rebukes al-Dahhak and counters that the Prophet performed tamattu and the Companions did it with him, despite Umar's ban.
rows.anchor: قال سعد قد صنعها رسول الله وصنعناها معه

rows.speaker: أبو موسى
rows.claim: Abu Musa reports that the Prophet told a pilgrim without sacrificial animals to perform tawaf and sa'y, then leave ihram; Abu Musa followed this instruction.
rows.anchor: عن أبي موسى، قال قدمت على رسول الله

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar later explained his changed rite by saying they should follow the Book's command to complete Hajj and umrah and the Prophet's practice of remaining in ihram until sacrifice.
rows.anchor: قال أن نأخذ بكتاب الله فإن الله قال { وأتموا الحج والعمرة لله } ، وأن نأخذ بسنة نبينا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The report sets Ibn Abbas's command to perform tamattu against Ibn al-Zubayr's prohibition; Jabir says the practice originated with their performance alongside the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قال كان ابن عباس يأمر بالمتعة وكان ابن الزبير ينهى عنها فذكر ذلك لجابر بن عبد الله

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir recalls doing tamattu with the Prophet and says Umar later urged separating Hajj from umrah to complete each independently.
rows.anchor: على يدي دار الحديث تمتعنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فلما قام عمر قال

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: In Abu Musa's report, Umar calls tamattu a Sunnah of the Prophet but says he fears pilgrims will have sex with their partners and return to Hajj perfumed.
rows.anchor: عن أبي موسى أن عمر قال هي سنة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يعني المتعة ولكني أخشى

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab reports Umar's ban and rationale: tamattu lets pilgrims enjoy comfort, sex, perfume, and clothes before Hajj, while Mecca's residents depend on visiting pilgrims for livelihood.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب أن عمر بن الخطاب نهى عن المتعة في أشهر الحج وقال فعلتها مع رسول الله

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir reports Umar's declaration that both forms of muta occurred under the Prophet but he would prohibit and punish them, including temporary marriage and Hajj tamattu.
rows.anchor: عن أبي نضرة عن جابر، قال قلت إن ابن الزبير ينهي عن المتعة

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar says he prohibits tamattu despite its being in God's Book and the Prophet having practiced it, meaning umrah within Hajj.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال سمعت عمر يقول والله إني لأنهاكم عن المتعة وإنها لفي كتاب الله

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: Uthman forbids tamattu while Ali commands it; Uthman answers Ali's reminder that they practiced it with the Prophet by saying they had been afraid.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شقيق، قال كان عثمان ينهي عن المتعة وكان علي يأمر بها

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr reports that Hajj tamattu, and both temporary marriage and Hajj tamattu, were permitted only to Muhammad's Companions.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ذر كانت المتعة في الحج لأصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai limits his inquiry to whether reported arguments for the ban follow Scripture or Sunnah; deciding whether the prohibitor was justified in his authority is a theological question outside this commentary's purpose.
rows.anchor: لكنا اقتصرنا منها على ما له دخل في غرضنا وهو البحث التفسيري عن نهيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to complete Hajj and umrah requires completion after undertaking them; it does not establish that umrah must be separated from Hajj or that combining them was exclusive to the Prophet or the Farewell Pilgrimage party.
rows.anchor: لا يدل على أزيد من وجوب إتمام الحج والعمرة بعد فرضهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's clause about being prevented supports completion after initiation, not the claim that tamattu is forbidden.
rows.anchor: والدليل عليه قوله تعالى { فإن أحصرتم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Claiming the practice was Prophet-only concedes that tamattu was his Sunnah, as Umar's own statement reported from Ibn Abbas confirms.
rows.anchor: وفيه مع ذلك اعتراف بأن التمتع كان سنة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Musa's appeal to the Book and Sunnah fails: the Qur'an supports tamattu, while the claim that the Prophet's Sunnah was to remain in ihram conflicts with other reports and explicit accounts of his tamattu.
rows.anchor: فقد عرفت أن الكتاب يدل على خلافه، وأما أن ترك التمتع سنة النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن تيمية
rows.claim: Ibn Taymiyya claims the Prophet performed qiran and that tamattu could refer to qiran; al-Tabatabai calls this a remarkable assertion.
rows.anchor: ومن عجيب الدعوى في هذا المقام ما ادعاه ابن تيمية أن حج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان حج قران وأن المتعة كانت تطلق على حج القران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not shaving until the sacrifice arrives does not prove entry into Hajj; the verse says a person carrying sacrifice and living outside the sanctuary must nonetheless be a tamattu pilgrim.
rows.anchor: مجرد عدم حلق الرأس حتى يبلغ الهدي محله ليس إحراما للحج ولا يثبت به ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the Prophet personally performed another form, he commanded all his Companions to perform tamattu; a practice ordered for the community cannot be treated as uniquely personal.
rows.anchor: هب أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أتى بغير التمتع لكنه أمر جميع أصحابه ومن معه بالتمتع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Banning tamattu because its release brings sex, perfume, and fine clothes into the pilgrim's experience is personal reasoning against an explicit divine and prophetic ruling.
rows.anchor: ففيه أنه اجتهاد في مقابل النص وقد نص الله ورسوله على الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse itself describes tamattu as taking enjoyment from umrah until Hajj, including lawful pleasures such as sex and clothing that the ban's proponents feared.
rows.anchor: فهل التمتع إلا استيفاء الحظ من المتاع والالتذاذ بطيبات النكاح واللباس وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Companions raised the same sexual objection when the verse was revealed; the Prophet rebuked them and reiterated tamattu as God's prescribed command.
rows.anchor: قلنا أيروح أحدنا إلى عرفة وفرجه يقطر منيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that tamattu harms Mecca's markets is personal reasoning against revelation; the Qur'an answers the analogous fear of economic hardship by promising God's provision when barring polytheists from the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: ففيه أيضا أنه اجتهاد في مقابل النص، على أن الله سبحانه يرد عليه في نظير المسأله بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamattu is not restricted to fear or impediment: the verse is unqualified, and its operative rule is the clause for those whose families do not live near the Sacred Mosque.
rows.anchor: ففيه أن الآيه مطلقة تشمل الخائف وغيره

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr defines tamattu as a Hajj pilgrim forced by enemy, illness, injury, or another impediment to turn the rite into umrah and defer Hajj until the next year.
rows.anchor: عن ابن الزبير أنه خطب فقال يا أيها الناس والله ما التمتع بالعمرة إلى الحج كما تصنعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that tamattu was a special allowance only for the Prophet's Companions fails because the verse's general wording covers everyone whose family is not resident at the Sacred Mosque; reports of Companions refusing it also contradict exclusivity.
rows.anchor: ففيه أنه مدفوع بإطلاق قوله تعالى { ذلك لمن لم يكن أهله حاضري المسجد الحرام }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final argument says the leader prohibited tamattu under his authority, invoking God's command to obey those in authority.
rows.anchor: وقد فرض الله طاعة أولي الأمر إذ قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scripture repeatedly requires following revelation and the Messenger's divinely authorized commands; in the contrast between what he gives and forbids, giving means commanding, so both must be obeyed.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالإيتاء الأمر بقرينة مقابلته بقوله وما نهاكم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience also covers God's and the Messenger's judgments: refusing to rule by revelation is called injustice, sin, or disbelief, and believers have no choice after their decree; God's choosing includes judgment and legislation.
rows.anchor: ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الظالمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Qur'an is protected from falsehood, its rulings remain until Resurrection and bind rulers and subjects alike; therefore leaders cannot change revealed law.
rows.anchor: وقد نص القرآن على أنه كتاب غير منسوخ وان الأحكام باقية على ما هي عليها إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obedience due to leaders concerns matters outside revealed law: they and the community must preserve divine rulings, while leaders may direct actions and restraint according to public interests within those rulings.
rows.anchor: إنما يجعل لأولي الأمر حق الطاعة في غير الأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Individuals may choose among lawful options, such as eating, trading, seeking a court, or waiving a defense; they cannot choose forbidden acts such as wine, usury, or seizing property.
rows.anchor: وليس له أن يشرب الخمر، ولا له أن يأخذ الربا، ولا له أن يغصب مال غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise, leaders may manage public affairs, including defense, public shutdowns, and spending, according to general interests while preserving God's rules.
rows.anchor: كذلك ولي الأمر له أن يتصرف في الأمور العامة على طبق المصالح الكلية مع حفظ الأحكام الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anything an individual may discretionarily do while preserving God's ruling may also be managed by the Prophet's deputy according to public benefit, with that ruling intact.
rows.anchor: فلولي الأمر من قبل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يتصرف فيه بحسب الصلاح العام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If rulers could alter religious obligations or permissions whenever current conditions seemed to warrant it, no law would remain stable and the Qur'an's continuing validity would be meaningless.
rows.anchor: لم يقم حكم على ساق، ولم يكن لاستمرار الشريعه إلى يوم القيامة معنى البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating tamattu as unsuitable by contemporary standards would similarly justify ignoring scriptural permissions for enslavement or punishments; this reductio shows leaders cannot suspend divine rulings for convenience.
rows.anchor: فما الفرق بين أن يقول قائل إن حكم التمتع من طيبات الحياة لا يلائم هيئة النسك والعبادة

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reports that when Umar considered banning Hajj tamattu, Ubayy ibn Ka'b said he had no authority because revelation established it and they performed it with the Prophet; Umar then relented.
rows.anchor: فقام إليه أبي بن كعب، فقال ليس ذلك لك قد نزل بها كتاب الله واعتمرنا مع رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an uses heart for the inner moral self, as in its descriptions of a sinful heart and a penitent heart; heart can then stand metaphorically for the self, and chest for the place of inner faculties.
rows.anchor: وفي القرآن شيء كثير من هذا الباب، قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People infer that the heart is life's source because consciousness may disappear in fainting or seizures while heartbeat and life continue; the soul first attaches to the heart and then extends throughout the body.
rows.anchor: والحياة المدلول عليها بحركة القلب ونبضانه باقية بخلاف القلب قطع على أن مبدأ الحياة هو القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Feeling, will, love, hatred, hope, and fear are attributed to the heart because it is the soul's first bodily locus, even though each organ begins its specialized task as an instrument.
rows.anchor: وأن الآثار والخواص الروحية كالإحساسات الوجدانية مثل الشعور، والإرادة، والحب، والبغض، والرجاء، والخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Experiments said birds can lose their brains and perception yet remain alive until nutrition fails and the heart stops, supporting the distinction between cognition and the source of life.
rows.anchor: أن الطيور لا تموت بفقد الدماغ إلا أنها تفقد الإدراك ولا تشعر بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Natural science has not identified the body's central command source; despite their separate actions, its organs obey one ruler in a real unity.
rows.anchor: إذ لا ريب أنها في عين التشتت والتفرق من حيث أنفسها وأفعالها مجتمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing inner faculties to the heart does not reflect ignorance of the brain: languages have long used head metaphors for authority and beginnings, while heart came to mean soul or self and chest the site of inner faculties.
rows.anchor: ولا ينبغي أن يتوهم أن ذلك كان ناشئا عن الغفلة عن أمر الدماغ وما يخصه من الفعل الإدراكي
